s1.syndrome_frame: Acute severe abdominal pain with nausea, transient loss of consciousness, and lethargy in a patient with a history of polycythemia vera and hypertension
key_facts: 14-year history of polycythemia vera
History of hypertension
Medications included aspirin, hydroxyurea, and intermittent losartan
Poor adherence to phlebotomies and other therapy
Blood pressure was 110/75 mmHg on arrival
Lethargic and confused on arrival
Chronic leukocytosis consistent with underlying disease
Abdominopelvic CT scan showed splenomegaly and bilateral adrenal masses
Adrenal masses were nonenhancing with an attenuation of 50 HU
No evidence of vascular thrombosis

shortlist.label: Adrenal Hemorrhage
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses with nonenhancing attenuation of 50 HU on CT scan

shortlist.label: Splenic Infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Splenomegaly and chronic leukocytosis consistent with polycythemia vera, with acute abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses, although nonenhancing, could be a rare presentation of pheochromocytoma

shortlist.label: Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral adrenal masses, which could be a rare but possible presentation of adrenal cortical carcinoma

shortlist.label: Splenomegaly due to Polycythemia Vera
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a 14-year history of polycythemia vera, which is a known cause of splenomegaly

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with acute severe abdominal pain, nausea, and transient loss of consciousness, combined with the imaging findings of bilateral nonenhancing adrenal masses, is most consistent with adrenal hemorrhage, particularly in the context of a patient with a history of polycythemia vera and potential for bleeding complications due to aspirin use and poor adherence to phlebotomies.

rejected.label: Splenic Infarction
rejected.why: While the patient has splenomegaly due to polycythemia vera, the primary complaint and imaging findings are more suggestive of an adrenal issue rather than a splenic one.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: The adrenal masses are nonenhancing and do not have the typical characteristics of pheochromocytoma on imaging, and there is no mention of symptoms suggestive of catecholamine excess.

rejected.label: Adrenal Cortical Carcinoma
rejected.why: The acute presentation and nonenhancing nature of the adrenal masses are not typical for adrenal cortical carcinoma, which usually presents with more chronic symptoms and has different imaging characteristics.

rejected.label: Splenomegaly due to Polycythemia Vera
rejected.why: While the patient does have splenomegaly due to polycythemia vera, this diagnosis does not explain the acute abdominal pain or the bilateral adrenal masses found on imaging.
